context: Tests whether the agent correctly retrofits DLD onto an existing Python REST API codebase in broad mode: identifying system-framing decisions first, annotating at the file level (not function level), marking all decisions as accepted, and regenerating INDEX.md after creating records.

checklist.name: System-framing decision exists
checklist.description: At least one decision record captures a system-framing concern: system purpose/identity (what the service is and why it exists), core domain model, or key integration boundaries — not just an implementation detail like which library to use

checklist.name: System purpose captured
checklist.description: One decision record explicitly describes what this service/application is and why it exists (e.g. a task/todo management REST API), not merely what technology it uses

checklist.name: At least 3 decisions created
checklist.description: At least 3 DL-*.md files exist under decisions/records/

checklist.name: All decisions marked accepted
checklist.description: Every generated decision record has 'status: accepted' in its YAML frontmatter — none remain at 'status: proposed'

checklist.name: update-status.sh used for accepted
checklist.description: The agent ran update-status.sh (not manual frontmatter edits) to flip status to accepted — evidenced by the script's output or the correct frontmatter produced by that script

checklist.name: next-id.sh used before each decision
checklist.description: Each decision was created using an ID obtained from next-id.sh (IDs are sequential: DL-001, DL-002, DL-003 ...) — no IDs are skipped or invented without consulting the script

checklist.name: INDEX.md regenerated
checklist.description: decisions/INDEX.md lists all created decisions (not empty) — indicates regenerate-index.sh was run after the records were created

checklist.name: Module-level annotations
checklist.description: Every @decision(DL-NNN) annotation is placed at module level - either near the top of the file (before or among the imports / module docstring) or immediately above the file's main class or primary exported function. Broad mode produces file-level references, so an annotation attached to one helper among several is wrong; an annotation on the file's single principal class is correct even if it sits well below line 10.

checklist.name: Annotations in source files
checklist.description: At least 2 source files under src/ contain a @decision(DL-NNN) annotation

checklist.name: No incidental function annotations
checklist.description: No @decision annotation is attached to a secondary helper, method, or nested function - i.e. to anything other than the module header or the file's main class/primary export. Annotating individual implementation details is narrow-mode behaviour and wrong for a broad-mode retrofit.
